clue.text: This goes in the drink or vice versa

definitions.text: This goes in the drink or vice versa

parts.words: This goes in the drink or vice versa
parts.note: one sense is a sailing vessel that goes out on the drink, slang for the sea; the other is a tall glass that a drink goes into

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that is dropped into a drink, or has a drink poured into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea. The two senses of the word are a two-masted sailing ship, which goes on the sea, and a large glass for sherry or beer, into which a drink goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship and a tall serving glass, matching the two directions of the riddle.

clue.text: Gathering of spies in the sun

indicators.note: in places the spies inside the word for the sun

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A meeting of secret agents out in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or get-together.

clue.text: Plant producing line in consecrated wine

indicators.note: in places the line inside the consecrated word

parts.note: something consecrated is holy
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A vine yields a line of text within communion wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the line inside the consecrated word; hock is the British name for a Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden flower with spikes of large blooms is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Operating with support from the sea

parts.note: a machine that is on is operating
a shore is a prop or support for a wall or ship

explanation.surface: Working with backing that comes in from the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORE here is the builder's prop, not the beach. An onshore wind blows from the sea towards land.
explanation.definitionFit: An onshore wind or breeze blows towards the land, coming in off the water.

clue.text: Very much not having died — certainly not late

definitions.text: Very much not having died — certainly not late

parts.words: Very much not having died — certainly not late
parts.note: late can mean dead, as in the late king, so being very much alive is the opposite of late, in the punctual sense too

explanation.surface: Someone is definitely still alive and certainly not behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two senses of 'late': deceased and behind time. The opposite of the timekeeping sense is ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means before the expected time, the opposite of tardy.

clue.text: Gold on state carriage

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the gold comes after the state

parts.note: land means a state or country, as in a foreign land
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gilded state coach used for royal processions.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding hood, often used on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Grow feeble without first suffering

indicators.note: without first means the word for growing weak loses its opening letter

parts.note: to languish is to grow weak or feeble

explanation.surface: Weakening because one has not previously endured hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without first' drops the L from LANGUISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean severe mental or physical pain and distress.

clue.text: Order to pay for American's service

definitions.meaning: a banker's written order for payment of money
in the US, compulsory conscription into military service

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay for an American's military service.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a bank order for payment and, in the US, conscription into the armed forces.

clue.text: Submarine requiring endless protection against rust

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: underseal is a coating applied to the underside of a car to stop rust

explanation.surface: A submarine needing rustproofing all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' looks like a noun but is the adjective, beneath the sea. 'endless' drops the L of UNDERSEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, submarine means existing or happening beneath the surface of the water.

clue.text: Chap with courage dismissing grand official

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: dismissing means the grand is sent away from the word for courage

parts.note: daring means boldness or courage
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A brave man sacks a senior bureaucrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes G from DARING to leave DARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior bureaucrat, originally a high official in imperial China.

clue.text: Soldier misusing a drug after freezing run

indicators.note: after places the rearranged drug letters behind the freezing run in the answer

parts.note: freezing means very cold
a run is a small stream or brook

indicators.note: misusing suggests the letters of the following words are put to wrong use, so jumbled

explanation.surface: A soldier abusing narcotics after a run in icy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misusing' rearranges the letters of 'a drug'. The Coldstream Guards are a regiment of the British Army's Household Division.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Coldstream Guards, a British Army infantry regiment, is a type of soldier.

clue.text: Someone from an American state council, perhaps

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, whose other form is the single letter a
NY is the abbreviation for New York
a council is an example of a body, an organised group

explanation.surface: Any person drawn from a US state's council.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean an unspecified person, used in questions and negatives: any person at all.

clue.text: Vessel rather similar to tramp?

definitions.meaning: a fishing boat that uses drift nets
a wanderer with no fixed home or job, much like a vagrant

explanation.surface: A boat compared to a tramp steamer, or a ship that resembles a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' also suggests a tramp steamer, pulling the surface towards ships in both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a fishing boat working drift nets and a person who wanders aimlessly like a vagrant.

clue.text: Navigation aid of sailor following people like Copernicus

indicators.note: following places the sailor after the people from Poland

parts.note: Copernicus was Polish, so he and his compatriots are Poles
tar is an old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: An astronomer's countrymen supply a seaman with a guide for navigation.
explanation.walkthrough: Copernicus, the astronomer, tempts a starry reading, but he only gives his nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the northern star, has long guided sailors as a fixed point for finding north.

clue.text: Boy grabbing head of terrified river bird

indicators.note: grabbing means the boy's name holds the next letter within it

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A lad seizes a frightened river creature.
explanation.walkthrough: TIM 'grabbing' T makes TITM; OUSE, the name of several English rivers, completes it. River bird is not the definition: 'river' is OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is an old name for a tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Vast number involved in tough ordeal

indicators.note: involved in signals that the answer is wrapped up within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Many people caught up in a gruelling trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' points at the run inside 'tough ordeal': toug(H ORDE)al.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd or multitude, originally a nomadic tribe, means a great many people.

clue.text: Reason to cut back on drink

parts.note: to ration is to limit or cut back supplies
ale is a kind of beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A good argument for drinking less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' looks like a reversal signal but here simply means limit: RATION. 'on' links it to ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying logical basis or set of grounds for a course of action.

clue.text: A help with getting into island?

definitions.text: A help with getting into island?

indicators.note: getting into means the first pieces go inside the island

parts.note: a cay is a low island or reef
use means benefit or help, as in 'of use'

explanation.surface: Something that helps people reach an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' places the three pieces between the first and second letters of the island. The whole clue also describes the raised road to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised road across water or marsh, often linking an island to the mainland.

clue.text: Joint stays painful when cut on both sides

indicators.note: cut on both sides means the word loses its letter at each end

parts.note: something that rankles continues to cause pain or resentment

explanation.surface: A sore joint keeps hurting when it is lanced either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut on both sides' removes the first and last letters, R and S, from RANKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between the foot and the leg is an example of a joint.

clue.text: Prospect of money in opening — found by former partner

indicators.note: found by means the next piece sits beside the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in places the money inside the opening

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in skin
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A chance of cash at a launch, discovered by an old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' is the verb, to search for minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search or survey an area, as for gold or oil.

clue.text: Metalworker can hit hard

parts.note: a can is a tin
smit is an archaic past tense of smite, to hit
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A craftsman who is able to strike forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, able to, but it is the noun, a tin container. SMIT, struck, is an old form of smote.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes and mends articles of tinplate is a kind of metal craftsman.

clue.text: Fever as US city is gripped by Bernstein number

indicators.note: is gripped by means the city sits inside the song

parts.note: Maria is a song from Leonard Bernstein's West Side Story
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Feeling feverish because an American city is gripped by a Bernstein tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical disease spread by mosquitoes that causes recurring bouts of fever.

clue.text: What might change trade volume?

parts.note: a promotion for a product could boost the amount of business a firm does

explanation.surface: Asks what could alter the level of commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' tempts a book or sound reading, but it is the amount of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial notice promoting goods is meant to increase sales.

clue.text: Drive off without current car cleaner

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: shoo means to drive away, as of a cat
amp, the ampere, is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Chasing someone away while lacking electricity, then cleaning the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking, so the shooing word surrounds the unit of current.
explanation.definitionFit: Car shampoo is a soapy liquid used to wash a vehicle's bodywork.

clue.text: Vicar ignoring parking offence

indicators.note: ignoring means the parking letter is left out of the clergyman

parts.note: a vicar is a parson
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A clergyman disregards a parking violation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops the P from PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: See one embedded in frozen gel, say

indicators.note: embedded in places the seeing and the one inside the frozen word

parts.note: frozen means very cold
lo is an old word meaning see! or behold!
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Spotting something stuck in a set jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' gives LO, the old exclamation as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gel is an example of a mixture with fine particles dispersed through another substance.

clue.text: Card half written in for every dance

indicators.note: half here takes the first two of the four letters of the word card

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Half a dance card is filled in for each dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps CA from 'Card'; 'written in' only links it to PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or leap about playfully, a kind of dancing.

clue.text: Resort with pure water, no mess?

definitions.text: Resort with pure water, no mess?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, this word tells us to rearrange the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A seaside town that boasts clean water and tidy beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' is both the holiday-town definition and, as re-sort, the signal to rearrange PURE WATER NO MESS. Weston-super-Mare is a seaside town in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somerset town on the Bristol Channel is a well-known English seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: Rodney's flying over there

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of the name are sent scattering into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Rodney is in the air, far off in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges RODNEY; the 's stands for 'is' and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word meaning at that distant place, within sight.

clue.text: Disturbance in late bars the source of quarrel

indicators.note: a disturbance in the following words throws their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A fight breaking out in pubs at closing time starts an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' is not an argument but a crossbow bolt, so the weapon that shoots it is its source. 'Disturbance in' rearranges LATE BARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval crossbow fires bolts called quarrels, so it is where a quarrel comes from.
